t: #3821 Find Nth Smallest Integer With K One Bits — Combinatorial Ranking
o: We need the n-th smallest positive integer with exactly k set bits, answer < 2^50. Integers with k ones grouped by their highest bit p: there are C(p, k-1) of them (choose the other k-1 ones among the p lower bits). Find the bucket containing rank n, then reconstruct the remaining bits greedily from high to low: numbers with the current candidate bit equal to 0 come first (there are C(b, rem) of them), so subtract that count when skipping a 0 and place a 1 otherwise. Example: n=4, k=2 -> buckets give highest bit 3 with rank 1 inside, yielding 1001 = 9.
k: Count of k-one integers with highest bit p is C(p, k-1); these buckets are contiguous in sorted order.
Within a fixed highest bit, numbers with the next candidate bit = 0 precede those with it = 1, and there are C(b, rem) of the former.
All binomials fit in 64-bit since C(50,25) ≈ 1.26e14.

a.i: Rank n against cumulative bucket sizes C(p, k-1) to find the highest set bit, then build the answer bit by bit from that bit downward using the same counting argument, consuming rank as we decide each bit.
s: Scan p = k-1, k, ... subtracting C(p, k-1) from n until n fits in a bucket; that p is the top bit.
Set the top bit, rem = k-1; for b from p-1 down to 0: if r > C(b, rem) skip the bit (r -= C(b, rem)), else set it and rem--.
a.t: O(50^2) precomputation plus O(50) reconstruction — effectively constant.

w: This is the standard 'unranking' technique for combinatorial objects in colex order. Common pitfalls: off-by-one in bucket boundaries (use 1-indexed rank carefully), confusing C(b, rem) with C(b, rem-1) during reconstruction, and 32-bit overflow in C++/Java. A follow-up might ask for the k-th smallest in a range, solved by the same counting with prefix adjustments.
